content.text: Abnorm opening in the atrial septum b/n the Rt & Lt atrium
allows for a Lt → Rt shunt
(CVA from venous clots) or dysrhythmias later in life
wide fixed split S2 that does ⍉vary w/ respirations
•Crochetage sign (notching of the peak of the R wave in the inferior leads)
Persistent communication b/n the descending thoracic aorta & main pulm a. after birth
continued prostaglandin E1 prod & lower arterial O2 content promoted patency
pulm HTN & cyanotic Hdz occurring when a L→R shunt switches & becomes a R→L shunt (cyanotic)
) first line to close a PDA in infants (PG inhibitor)
Congenital narrowing of the aortic lumen @ the dist or descending aorta
(70%), MV defects, patent ductus arteriosus, Turner syndrome

•narrowing of the aorta MC @ the insertion of the ductus arteriosus dist to the origin of the Lt subclavian v. results in HTN in the arteries prox to the lesion (ex, primary arteries supplying the UE) w/ relative hypotension in the LE
•over time, the body compensates by developing collaterals around the coarctation (ex, IC arteries)
: narrowing occurs dist to the ductus arteriosum
: narrowing occurs prox to the ductus arteriosum
May range from aSx to HF or shock after birth w/ closure of the patent ductus arteriosus
Systol BP in UE > than in LE
Systol murmur radiating to the back, scapula, or chest
(narrowed aorta looks like the notch of the # 3)
- balloon angioplasty w/ or w/o stent placement
- maintains a patent ductus arteriosus, reducing sxs & improves the LE blood flow
